proof_repairs.defect: qual_m4_2_e2e_006 phase B staged docs/54 fault 10 with a fixed MODBIT_COMPACTION_WORKER_DELAY_MS sleep and a 100 ms model pace, and asserted that a SYNC_FALLBACK epoch opened. The sleep races the turn rate, not the history, and loses both ways: on a slow host the 1.5 s elapses inside a turn or two, so compaction_step harvests the worker at stage 1 and installs its result as an ASYNC epoch, the transcript drops below the budget and the hard-pressure branch never runs (the observed failure: every ContextEpochOpened carried mode ASYNC); with a longer sleep the run ends first and every request is closed RUN_ENDED, failing the stale-rejection assertion instead. No value of the knob is safe on every runner. The product behaved correctly in the failing run; only the staging was wrong.
proof_repairs.audit: PRODUCTION-WORKING. The defect was in the proof, not the product: the fault hook and the test's preconditions, not compaction_step's hard/soft/harvest logic, which is unchanged.
proof_repairs.fix: The hook waits on state. A worker holds its result until the result can no longer install — an epoch opened without it (CompactionWorker::released, set by the hard branch right after install_epoch) or the run ended (set beside the existing abort, so a hold cannot outlive the run). The worker is therefore never harvested before hard pressure however slow the host, and what it returns is stale rather than RUN_ENDED. The env value survives only as the last-resort bound on a release that never comes; the test passes 60 s and nothing waits for it. compaction_scenario loses its pace parameter. Production is untouched: compaction_worker_hold() is None unless the fault variable is set, so the hold never runs and the flag is never read.
proof_repairs.assertions_changed: None. No assertion was weakened, removed or ignored; the phase B assertion set is byte-identical. An ordering assertion drafted during the fix was dropped as decorative — it is implied by the existing fallback and late assertions and cannot fail independently.
